items.excerpt: UW-Madison researchers trained a machine-learning model on high-throughput phage mutation data; it predicted mutations that let bacteriophages infect hosts up to a million times more effectively, validated in the lab (Cell Systems).
items.title: AI-guided mutations help viruses infect bacteria up to 1 million times more effectively

items.excerpt: EMBL-EBI and Google DeepMind, with NVIDIA, Seoul National University and others, added AI-predicted structures for more than 2,800 viruses to the AlphaFold Database to speed up vaccine and diagnostic target discovery.
items.title: New AlphaFold Database release adds viral protein complexes to support pandemic preparedness

items.excerpt: Anthropic says ~950 Claude agent sessions working over 21 hours found ART, a previously unknown CRISPR-like enzyme system with DNA repeat arrays in bacteriophages. The preprint has not been peer-reviewed.
items.title: Anthropic touts AI-led biology discovery

items.excerpt: UC Riverside researchers found that confidence and correctness in LLMs come from distinct internal features. Suppressing specific features raised accuracy and let the model flag unreliable answers with 81% accuracy.
items.title: Making AI more trustworthy by making it red-flag its own doubtful answers

items.excerpt: UC Berkeley and Princeton's TANGO vision-language framework controls all 29 joints of a humanoid from language instructions and camera images. It was trained on 65k synthetic trajectories and doubled success rates over 2D path planning.
items.title: Humanoid robots navigate narrow gaps and obstacles with whole-body AI control

items.excerpt: Harvard SEAS and Georgia Tech released RLE-Bench, 48 simulated tasks that test whether AI coding agents can handle the full engineering of working robots: control, perception, policy and mechanical design.
items.title: Open-source benchmark tests whether AI agents can engineer working robots

items.excerpt: Michigan State University's AI, trained on US worker chest X-rays, detects early pneumoconiosis with 91% accuracy versus 77% for human readers, easing a shortage of about 200 specialist B readers (Occupational and Environmental Medicine).
items.title: AI innovation supports screening for 2.2 million US workers exposed to toxic dust

items.excerpt: QC Design reports that its Meridian AI system achieved logical error rates more than 10x lower than published methods across 100+ quantum design tasks.
items.title: QC Design Reports 10x Logical Error Reduction With Meridian AI

items.excerpt: A theoretical quantum-emitter nanostructure could supply the nonlinear operations that energy-efficient optical neural networks need.
items.title: Tiny Quantum Nanostructures Could Make AI Less of an Energy Hog

items.excerpt: Can a six-dimensional sphere be described using imaginary numbers? Experts puzzled over this for decades, and now an AI has apparently answered it.
items.title: AI solves 79-year-old math mystery of six-dimensional spheres

items.excerpt: Chess grandmasters move toward less complex positions faster than AI engines, which hold complex positions for longer. The two appear to balance short- and long-term prospects in different ways (Physics 19, 126).
items.title: Chess Reveals Differences Between Human and AI Strategies

items.excerpt: University of Washington students tested Ai2's AutoDiscovery. It can surface promising scientific leads, but that makes human judgment, domain expertise and rigorous validation more important, not less.
items.title: Teaching future scientists to interrogate AI tools for scientific discovery

items.excerpt: A crowdsourced game built on Olmo 3 showed people exploiting unexpected model behaviors to stress-test prosocial AI evaluations, and how open model internals help explain why those tests break.
items.title: What a crowdsourced game revealed about steering Olmo 3

items.excerpt: Google Research treats long-form video generation as a global optimization problem, using a multi-agent framework (AI co-director, CANVAS, A2RD, VQQA) to fight character drift and cascading failures.
items.title: Automating coherent long-form video generation

items.excerpt: Generative AI and papermills are flooding journals with fraudulent papers, and publishers are responding with new detection tools and integrity checks.
items.title: How scientific publishers are fighting back against fraudulent papermills

items.excerpt: A new wave of radiology practices is embracing AI aggressively, developing and deploying models in-house. (STAT+ paywalled)
items.title: In radiology, AI is blurring the line between technology development and clinical practice

items.excerpt: You can close an AI chat and walk into a meeting in seconds, but shifting from instant responses to listening, patience and shared attention takes longer.
items.title: From Working With AI to Connecting With People
